I LOVE the idea of family traditions. We didn't have too many when I was a kid, but what we did do, I definitely remember. One was, every Sunday after church, we'd go on a long drive around the North Shore (grew up in Hawaii, so picture farmland, then beaches and green tropical foliage covering the mountainsides that you're driving on.) Loved those days.

I was actually talking to a friend last night about what traditions we'd want to start with our own families. A few ideas being Advent Calendars, Christmas Eve Boxes (a box with new p.j,s hot cocoa, and snacks for holiday movies,) and making ornaments with our kids every year. Admittedly, we did get these ideas from Pintrest, but it's a start to get the ball rolling.

I wouldn’t worry about where the ideas come from (Pintrest or wherever). Some of my favorite childhood memories are from one family tradition that our parents didn’t even intentionally realize they were creating.

It wasn’t until years later as adults when my brother called it a family tradition that we recognized that’s what it really had been.

I think it’s more about making memories and feeling a family connection than where (or how) it originated.
